## The question

How should a result travel from analysis to a talk?

- Preserve the argument.
- Make uncertainty visible.
- Keep the source reproducible.

::: notes
This standard Reveal note stays hidden while presenting, is available to
speaker view and Slide Remote, and appears in the handout PDF.
:::

# Evidence

## A result with context

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}

::: {.aside}
Illustrative values used to exercise layout; they are not empirical claims.
:::

::: notes
The handout stacks this speaker note and the visible aside without overlap.
:::

## Fragments collapse in PDFs

::: {.incremental}
1. Define the estimand.
2. Show the identifying variation.
3. Report uncertainty.
:::

::: notes
Both PDF variants contain the final state once, not one page per fragment.
:::

## Staged code highlighting

```{.r code-line-numbers="1|2-3|4"}
model <- lm(outcome ~ treatment, data = sample)
estimate <- coef(model)[["treatment"]]
interval <- confint(model)["treatment", ]
c(estimate = estimate, lower = interval[1], upper = interval[2])
```

::: notes
Handout mode does not leave unselected code lines dimmed.
:::

## Tables remain readable

| Specification | Estimate | Standard error |
|:--------------|---------:|---------------:|
| Baseline      | 0.18     | 0.06           |
| Controls      | 0.17     | 0.06           |
| Fixed effects | 0.15     | 0.07           |

## Explicit dark background {.dark-bg background-color="#1e293b"}

Text color is opt-in for dark backgrounds.

- Links remain [distinguishable](https://quarto.org/).
- Emphasis does not depend on color alone.

## Light custom background {.light-bg background-color="#ffeac2"}

Light backgrounds never inherit white text merely because a background color exists.

# Conclusion

## What the format promises

- Markdown and computation remain Quarto-native.
- Presentation and handout artifacts come from the same rendered deck.
- The default design is opinionated; the YAML remains easy to edit.
